key_insight: Temperature can substitute for process quality: thermally activated leakage with Ea ~0.3 eV falls ~1e14 from 300 to 77 K, so crude TFTs could hold charge.
killer_doubt: Grain-boundary field-assisted tunnelling is nearly temperature-independent (expect ~1e2, not 1e6). IGZO already leaks <1e-18 A/um at 300 K, and 77 K costs 9.7-19.3 W per W.
decisive_experiment: Cryoprobe Ioff distributions of 10^4 SPC poly-Si TFTs (to the 1e-6 tail) at 300/150/77 K and Vds 0.3-1.5 V, beside IGZO TFTs on the same glass. ~$60k.
prior_art: Cryogenic DDR3 4,096 s at 77 K (JSTS 2022); IGZO 2T0C 8,000 s at 77 K (2025); Phase B N-94 cold oxide gain cells.

key_insight: Retired server DRAM has no dominant cell wear-out. Recovered bits use no wafer capacity and arrive in months, a real supply lever during a 4x price spike.
killer_doubt: Desoldering adds a ~260 C reflow, ~1-3% package loss and rework cost for no gain: DDR4 CXL controllers (Marvell Structera X 2404, 12 DIMMs) take whole DIMMs.
decisive_experiment: Desolder and reball 1,000 packages from retired RDIMMs. Compare post-reflow BIST fallout, retention and VRT shift with the same lot tested as intact DIMMs. ~$80k; expect intact reuse to win.
prior_art: Meta Vistara CXL ASIC reusing retired DDR4 (2026) and Marvell Structera X 2404 DDR4-reuse controller (via search snippet); used-RDIMM resale market.

key_insight: Per-DIMM measured retention, hammer and timing bins written into SPD turn anonymous used DIMMs into graded CXL capacity tiers for buyers who are not hyperscalers.
killer_doubt: Feedstock. Hyperscalers (~half of server DRAM) now keep retired DDR4 internally (Meta Vistara), so open-market supply may be ~1-2 EB/yr against ~30+ EB/yr of new bits (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Buy 500 retired RDIMMs at auction. FPGA-profile each for 48 h (85 C retention, hammer threshold, VRT), run 50 behind a Structera-X CXL server for 6 months logging CE/UE, and survey ITAD volumes. ~$250k.
prior_art: Meta Vistara internal DDR4 reuse via CXL; Marvell Structera X 2404 (via search snippet); Microsoft GreenSKU (prior knowledge, unverified); refurbished-RDIMM resellers.

key_insight: Idle Gen-8.5 display fabs have ~60x a wafer's area per substrate and cheap PECVD and sputter tools. Oxide gain cells need no Czochralski silicon, crucible or EUV.
killer_doubt: Gen-8.5 steppers resolve ~1.5-2 um, not 0.5 um. At F=1.5 um a 16-tier panel holds ~0.3-0.5 TB at ~$10-20/GB, and ppm glass compaction breaks the tier overlay.
decisive_experiment: On a Gen-6 high-resolution line, build a 4-tier IGZO 2T gain-cell test panel at the tightest available rule. Measure tier-to-tier overlay, per-tier D0 and retention maps. ~$800k.
prior_art: ram-venture A1-03 (display-glass IGZO memory, killed on density). Phase B N-38 (Gen 3.5 panel, 64-128 tiers, imprint at 100 nm) is the better version.

key_insight: Correct first principle: DRAM has no dominant cell wear-out, so second-life bits are nearly as good as new and need no wafer capacity.
killer_doubt: Field data show correctable-error incidence rising with DIMM age (Schroeder 2009). Die-level harvest adds reflow loss and cost, and cannot make DDR4 dies serve DDR5 sockets.
decisive_experiment: Reball 1,000 harvested packages and compare BIST fallout and retention with intact DIMMs. Then age-stratify CE rates on 200 DIMMs over 3 months. ~$100k.
prior_art: Meta Vistara and Marvell Structera X reuse whole DDR4 DIMMs via CXL (via search snippet); Schroeder et al. 2009 DRAM field study (prior knowledge).

key_insight: The yield ramp burns depreciation (~55% of wafer cost). Shared defect taxonomies could cut root-cause time for entrants with no fab history.
killer_doubt: Ramp speed is set by learning cycles (~60-90-day DRAM cycle time, ~8-12 cycles in 24 months), not by classification. Recipe-specific defects transfer poorly between fabs.
decisive_experiment: Train a federated classifier across 3 university or pilot fabs plus WM-811K. Measure accuracy on a held-out fab's new defect classes against local-only training. ~$300k of software; the ramp claim itself stays untested.
prior_art: KLA and Applied automatic defect classification; PDF Solutions Exensio; academic federated wafer-map classification papers (prior knowledge).

key_insight: With periphery bonded separately, the cell wafer is purely periodic. Dry 193 nm two-beam fringes (~51 nm half-pitch) plus SAQP reach ~13 nm lines with no reticle or projection lens.
killer_doubt: Overlay. A perfect fringe grating cannot follow the 1-3 nm intra-die wafer distortion that scanners correct with high-order models, and array layers need <=2.5 nm overlay.
decisive_experiment: On a Lloyd's-mirror or SBIL tool, print two stacked gratings plus a crossed hole layer on 300 mm wafers with moire phase alignment. Map overlay and LER against a 2.5 nm budget. ~$500k.
prior_art: MIT scanning-beam interference lithography (Nanoruler); Eulitha displacement Talbot lithography; Phase B N-32 is the same idea (prior knowledge).

key_insight: A 16-32-cell local bitline (~0.6-1 fF) driving a local gain FET swings ~250-300 mV from a 1 fF cell, so the capacitor can be ~5x shorter (AR ~70 to ~15).
killer_doubt: VCT gain-FET sigma-Vt of ~30-50 mV against a ~250 mV end-of-retention signal gives only ~5-6 sigma over 1e10 cells. A buried-bitline-to-gate contact likely costs one critical mask.
decisive_experiment: Run SPICE Monte Carlo on a calibrated VCT model. Then build a university 1T1C-MIM test array of 16-cell segments with 3T local amplifiers, and measure the signal, offset tail and restore. ~$600k.
prior_art: IBM SOI eDRAM micro sense amplifier on 32-cell local bitlines (Barth, ISSCC 2007-08); Phase B N-90, N-40 and N-61 (prior knowledge).

key_insight: IBM's native sequence makes the deep trench first, so a pre-capacitored substrate is thermally compatible with a standard FEOL and lets fabs without memory lines host eDRAM-class arrays.
killer_doubt: Deep-trench cells (~0.03 um2) take ~20x commodity DRAM area, about 3 nm SRAM density. BEOL MIM eDRAM (Intel 22 nm) needs no substrate lock-in, and trench placement is product-specific.
decisive_experiment: Buy silicon trench-capacitor (PICS-style) wafers, run a 130-180 nm logic flow on top at SkyWater, and measure strap resistance, node leakage and alignment. ~$700k.
prior_art: IBM/GlobalFoundries deep-trench eDRAM (POWER7-9, z-series); Murata/IPDiA silicon trench capacitors; Intel 22 nm MIM eDRAM (prior knowledge).

key_insight: Few-electron storage needs no capacitor or deep etch. Per-cell write-verify and majority coding are the right tools for the random threshold scatter of grains.
killer_doubt: Current through 3-4 nm poly-Si grain channels is ~nA, so sensing takes microseconds. ~7e13 hot-row writes of 5 e- push ~1e8 C/cm2 through a few-nm2 barrier, beyond any Qbd.
decisive_experiment: Fabricate 1,000 Yano-type 3 nm poly-Si cells on a university line. Measure read current, Vt scatter after write-verify, retention at 85 C and endurance to 1e10 cycles. ~$300k.
prior_art: Hitachi/Yano poly-Si single-electron memory (1993-98); SunRise Memory quasi-volatile 3D NOR; nanocrystal flash (prior knowledge).

key_insight: If a qualified open gain-cell macro exists, every U.S. logic wafer start can carry memory without per-customer memory IP or NDA friction.
killer_doubt: Si gain cells in FinFET or GAA retain ~10-100 us at 85 C and give only ~1.5-2x HD-SRAM density. Leading foundries will not publish 18A or N4 macros openly.
decisive_experiment: Tape out a 2T/3T gain-cell macro on SkyWater 130 and GF 22FDX MPWs. Measure 85 C retention distributions, refresh power and bits/mm2 against foundry SRAM. ~$300k.
prior_art: Academic Si gain-cell eDRAM macros (Teman, Burg, Giterman); OpenRAM compiler; Phase B N-35 BEOL oxide gain cells (prior knowledge).

key_insight: Spin-on cyclopentasilane plus nanosecond laser crystallization makes a silicon tier from one coat and one scan, with no epitaxy or layer transfer.
killer_doubt: Laser poly-Si write FETs leak ~1e-13 to 1e-12 A: a 0.5 fF node with 0.2 V margin holds 0.1-1 ms, less in 85 C tails. IGZO leaks <1e-18 A/um.
decisive_experiment: Spin CPS films in a glovebox coater, laser-crystallize them and build 2T gain cells on two tiers. Map the 85 C Ioff tail and the lower-tier TFT shift after the upper-tier laser. ~$400k.
prior_art: Kovio printed-Si RFID (to 2014); Shimoda et al. solution-processed silicon TFTs (Nature 2006); CEA-Leti laser-annealed sequential 3D (prior knowledge).
